policy_suffix: The caller has already filtered the eligible candidates. IDs are opaque handles, not evidence of correspondence. Judge this direction independently; no reverse votes are supplied. Adjacency and option order do not establish a match. Examples illustrate the policy; they are not candidates.
candidate_meaning: This candidate supports the same source-grounded role as `focus`.
choice_question: Which candidate has the strongest defensible role correspondence with `focus`?
no_match_criterion: Every candidate performs a different role or lacks support for a shared role.
ranking_policy_omission:
Choose the strongest defensible correspondence, not the least-bad candidate.
Abstain when there is none.
ranking_question: Which candidate comes closest to the role and relevant relations of `focus`, even if none supports a defensible match? Selection alone does not assert a match.
has_match_question: Does at least one candidate in `candidates` support a defensible shared role with `focus`?
has_match_true: At least one candidate preserves the focus's role and relevant relations, supported by each represented paper.
has_match_false: All candidates perform different roles or lack source support; shared topics or question wording do not establish correspondence.
